title: DeMo: Decoupled Momentum Optimization
claim: Data is split into chunks, transformed to a frequency domain, sparsified by keeping top coefficients, then reconstructed with little information loss.
layout: 1 panel, left-to-right, grid tiles feeding labeled arrow operators
description: A single horizontal strip shows a left-to-right transform pipeline. At the far left is a 4x4 grid of blue-outlined square tiles, which are chunks of a tensor. One tile is expanded with converging lines into a larger blue 8x8 grid. A labeled arrow marked DCT leads to an orange grid of the same size, holding frequency coefficients. A second arrow marked TopK leads to a similar orange grid in which many cells are blanked to white, leaving only the largest coefficients. A third arrow marked IDCT leads to a green 8x8 grid. That grid expands out through lines into one tile of a 4x4 grid of green-outlined tiles at the far right, the reconstruction. Color changes mark each stage: blue, then orange, then green. The eye goes first to the colored grids in the middle.
caption: Chunk-wise Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT), top-$k$ coefficient selection, and inverse DCT reconstruction.
abstract: Scaling neural network training increasingly depends on synchronous data-parallelism, yet full-precision gradient all-reduce imposes a severe communication bottleneck. We propose Decoupled Momentum Optimization (DeMo), a drop-in replacement for any momentum-based optimizers that significantly reduces the communication bandwidth while maintaining convergence. DeMo (i) decouples local momentum updates, (ii) applies a fast orthonormal transform (e.g., DCT) followed by top-k sparsification, and (iii) reuses the momentum buffer as error feedback via momentum subtraction. This design reduces per-step communication by up to two orders of magnitude with minimal computational overhead. Experiments on 300M and 1B-parameter DeMo language models show DeMo transmits up to 85x less data per GPU than AdamW-DDP while achieving comparable loss and accuracy. DeMo is topology-agnostic and enables training across multi-datacenter or Ethernet-based setups. Code is available at https://github.com/bloc97/DeMo
